study.title: Category breadth and later cross-category purchasing (illustrative example)
study.research_question: Does a customer's earlier category breadth predict expansion into new categories in the following period?
study.target_population: Retail customers of one online fashion retailer
study.estimand: Difference in the number of newly purchased categories in months 7-12 between customers with higher vs lower category breadth in months 1-6, among customers active in months 1-6.

data_exposure.description: Read the data documentation and ran a structure-level profile with the outcome variable blinded. No distributions or trends of the outcome were viewed.

constructs.name: Category breadth
constructs.definition: Number of distinct product categories a customer bought from in the history window

constructs.name: Category expansion
constructs.definition: Number of categories bought in the outcome window that the customer had not bought in the history window

variables.label: Category breadth (history window)
variables.derivation: count of distinct product_category per customer in months 1-6

variables.label: New categories (outcome window)
variables.derivation: count of categories in months 7-12 not bought in months 1-6

variables.label: Total categories available
variables.derivation: number of categories in the catalogue; used to check the mechanical ceiling on expansion

sample_rules.frame: All customers with at least one order in months 1-6 of the study window
inclusion: at least one order in the history window

exclusion.rule: customers with a single order overall (cannot show expansion)
orders flagged as returned or cancelled

time_window.rationale: Chosen to end before the 2020 volume drop flagged by the profile; 2020 data reserved and not examined.

analysis_plan.hypothesis: H1: higher category breadth predicts more new categories in the outcome window
analysis_plan.model: Poisson or negative binomial regression of V_new_cats on V_breadth with V_total_cats as covariate; robust SEs
analysis_plan.notes: Report the mechanical ceiling check alongside the main estimate.

holdout_or_blinding.details: 2020 data are not examined until the 2019 analysis is finished; they serve as an out-of-time replication.

items_needing_human_verification: Data use terms of the public dataset (research use, redistribution)
Whether institutional ethics review or an exemption is required for pseudonymised retail data
Storage location and retention for the downloaded file
governance.storage_and_retention: Encrypted local disk; delete raw copy after project end unless terms allow retention.

conditions: Verify how product_category was defined and whether it changed over time

decision_log.basis: Structure-level profile flagged abnormal monthly record counts in 2020
